solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With noted talent for "Oklahoma!" say?

definitions.meaning: someone gifted with notes, i.e. good at music
Oklahoma! is an example of a stage ..., a noun here

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of talent suits a famous stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the adjective (gifted at music); the second is the noun, with 'say' marking Oklahoma! as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a gift for music is musical, and Oklahoma! is a classic Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of that genre.

clue.text: They may help to recall mobile Maria wrecked

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Souvenirs of Maria's mobile phone after it was smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges MOBILEMARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorabilia are keepsakes valued for the memories they bring back.

clue.text: Open all the time after resistance ended at front

parts.note: since means from then on, all the time after
R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: at front means only the leading letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An admission of honesty: always open since the resistance ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front' gives E, the first letter of ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere is open and genuine, without pretence.

clue.text: Ill-tempered promise — this?!

parts.note: cross means ill-tempered
word means a promise, as in 'I give you my word'

explanation.surface: An angry vow, with a self-referential nudge at the puzzle itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at the very thing the solver is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle being solved is itself a crossword, so 'this' refers to the answer.

clue.text: Jewellery item — severe reprimand when directions are reversed

indicators.note: reversing directions turns right into left, so the letter for one swaps for the other

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery earns a sharp telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: In ROCKET the R (right) becomes L (left). 'Getting a rocket' is British slang for being scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: A locket is a small pendant case, often holding a photo, worn as jewellery.

clue.text: Overtake father and sons

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A family on the road: dad and the boys get past someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a car on the road is to overtake it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pole needed to use ATM

definitions.meaning: the flagpole marking the hole on a golf green
the personal number keyed in at a cash machine

explanation.surface: A Polish person needing to use a cash machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is the stick on a golf green.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf flagstick is called the pin, and a personal identification number unlocks a cash card.

clue.text: Pay for exhibition area at fair

definitions.meaning: to ... someone a drink is to pay for it
an exhibitor's booth at a trade fair

explanation.surface: Paying for an exhibitor's space at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone means standing them a round; a booth at a show is also a stand.

clue.text: Fruit woman got, partly missing

indicators.note: partly missing means the outer bits of these words are missing, leaving a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A woman picked up some fruit, but part of it has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly missing' reads as a deletion instruction on each word, but the fruit simply sits inside 'woman got' once its ends are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a sweet tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Is able to vote as several standing initially seek support

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: An election scene: people able to vote, several standing for office, are out seeking support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' applies to all four following words, not just the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to go round asking people for their votes or backing, as campaigners do.

clue.text: Impressive revised arrangement of act? Clap? Sure!

indicators.note: a revised arrangement puts the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer asks whether a reworked act deserves applause, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised arrangement of' shuffles ACTCLAPSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectacular is striking and impressive to watch.

clue.text: Discourteous when daughter leaves leading to regret

indicators.note: when the daughter leaves, that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: rude means discourteous

explanation.surface: A rude remark made as the daughter walks out ends in regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes D from RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, as in 'rue the day'.

clue.text: Not half mocked in jockey's equipment? Leave fast!

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a saddle is what a jockey sits on

indicators.note: not half of the word means losing its first half, keeping only the back three letters

explanation.surface: Someone mocked over their riding kit is urged to get away quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps the back half of 'mocked', and 'in' places it after the first letter of the jockey's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is an informal word for running off in a hurry.

clue.text: New aid in coma — it's found in proteins

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A new medical aid for a coma patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges AIDINCOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks that link into chains to form proteins.

clue.text: British school language

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A British school teaching a language.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the well-known English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is the Celtic tongue spoken in Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Choice tips from expert getting post

parts.note: pick means choice, as in 'take your pick'

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A choice selection of tips from an expert lands someone a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips from' takes E and T, the ends of expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket is a pointed stake or post, as in a picket fence.

clue.text: Flier, quickest, relative displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A list of a fast creature and its kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon, a bird, and so a flier.

clue.text: Publicity, limitless, from computers etc that's skilful

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity

indicators.note: limitless means the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: IT is information technology, computing and the like

explanation.surface: Endless publicity from the tech world claims great skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' strips F and M from 'from', leaving RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means deft or clever with hands or mind.

clue.text: Resort everyone rejected — Northern failure? No

indicators.note: rejected, thrown back, means the word is turned round

parts.note: all means everyone
a dud is a failure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern resort turned down by everyone: is it a failure? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALL into LLA. Llandudno is a seaside resort town on the north coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a classic Victorian seaside holiday resort in North Wales.

clue.text: Fragrance of a capital (in local parlance)

parts.note: Roma is the Italians' own name for Rome, the capital

explanation.surface: The scent of a capital city, described as locals would.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell or fragrance.

clue.text: Dry a very short time

definitions.meaning: the French-derived term for dry wine
... is short for second, as in 'wait a ...'

explanation.surface: A dry spell that lasts hardly any time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec describes dry wine or champagne, and is also casual shorthand for a second.

clue.text: Fuss about vocal, never ending, Green?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ado means fuss, as in 'much ado about nothing'

indicators.note: never ending means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A fuss about someone vocal who never stops: an environmentalist?
explanation.walkthrough: 'never ending' trims the final L of 'vocal'; 'about' wraps the fuss round it. 'Green' looks like an eco-campaigner but is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a pale yellowish green, the colour of the fruit's flesh; the question mark flags this example.

clue.text: Suitable carpet oddly overlooked

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are passed over, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A suitable carpet, though some of it was missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipping C, R, E leaves A, P, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Song of Republican over in California

indicators.note: in puts the first two pieces inside the state

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A song about a Republican done with in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R and O inside CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a song, especially a festive Christmas hymn.

clue.text: Continue after all others

explanation.surface: Keep going until everyone else has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb last means endure, and the adjective means final in order.

clue.text: After time more unusual accepted learner's young child

indicators.note: after time means following the T, which therefore comes first
accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: odder means more unusual
L is the learner sign on British L-plates

explanation.surface: Over time a stranger learner was taken on: a young child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts L inside ODDER, giving ODDLER, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a child just learning to walk, roughly one to three years old.
